evals.prompt: While testing Evaluate Current Form inside rich comment blocks I noticed that a `(comment ...)` nested inside another `(comment ...)` is sent whole: with the cursor inside the inner comment's body, the whole inner `(comment ...)` form gets evaluated and returns nil, instead of the body form under the cursor like it does for a top-level comment block. I'm not fixing that in this PR. Note it for later.
evals.expected_output: A new docs/backlog/<slug>.md entry with title, Status: open, Problem citing src/repl/forms.ts, Fix or Why-left-alone, Origin; committed on its own; no code changes.
expectations: A new file was created under docs/backlog/ with a kebab-case name and no date or number in it
The file's first line is a '# ' title that states the observed behavior as a sentence, and the next non-blank line is exactly '**Status: open**'
The Problem section cites the code location by path (src/repl/forms.ts or the relevant function) rather than describing the symptom only
The file contains either a Fix / Proposed fix section or a 'Why it is left alone' section
The file has an Origin section saying where and when the issue surfaced
The entry was committed in its own commit (git-log shows a commit whose message says Backlog or docs: backlog) and no source file outside docs/ was modified

evals.prompt: what's in the backlog? and which one would you pick up first, and why
evals.expected_output: Lists all four open entries by title, no done entries, and recommends one with a value-vs-size rationale drawn from the entries' Fix sections.
expectations: The response lists all four open entries by title (format selection column offset, def-prefixed call highlighted as definition, jar scheme hardcoded, palette activation gate)
The response recommends one specific entry to pick up first with a rationale grounded in value versus size/effort from the entries' own Fix or Why-left-alone sections
No files were changed (git-status is empty)

evals.prompt: let's pick up the format-selection column offset issue from the backlog and plan it. I'm away for a few hours so don't wait on me for questions, make the calls yourself. Write the plan, but don't start implementing.
evals.expected_output: A plan in docs/plans/YYYY-MM-DD-HHMM-<topic>.md whose design carries over the backlog entry's fix and notes, cites the entry, and ends with a task closing it; the backlog entry status changed to planned with a Plan: line; no source code modified.
expectations: A plan file was created in docs/plans/ named YYYY-MM-DD-HHMM-<topic>.md (date and 4-digit time prefix)
The plan cites the backlog entry docs/backlog/format-selection-column-offset.md by path

The plan's design carries over the backlog entry's fix (pad the slice to the form's column, strip padding from output) and its notes (keep the glued-prefix walk, leave the whitespace-only branch, cover #?@ splicing in tests)
The plan includes a final task that closes the backlog entry (changes its status to done with a line saying where it landed)
The backlog entry's status line was changed from 'Status: open' to 'Status: planned' with a 'Plan: docs/plans/...' line pointing at the new plan
No source code under src/ was modified (only docs/ files changed)
